principles: A charge given to a ten-year-old
Gifts withdrawn from a whole people
A boy visited and then forbidden to speak

world_behind.title: The book names itself in its first sentence
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says he calls it the Book of Mormon.

world_behind.title: His qualification is observation
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has Ammaron call him a sober child, quick to observe. 4 Nephi 1:48 dates Ammaron hiding the records at three hundred and twenty years, which is the same year, so the custodian chose his successor on the day he buried the collection.

world_behind.title: The assignment is dated fourteen years out
world_behind.text: Verse 3 tells him to act when he is about twenty-four. Mormon 2:17 reports him going according to the word of Ammaron and taking the plates of Nephi, in the three hundred and forty-fifth year, which is fourteen years after the instruction and exactly on schedule.

world_behind.title: He is named for his father
world_behind.text: Verse 5 gives the father's name as Mormon too.

world_behind.title: The seven lineage names are back in use
world_behind.text: Verses 8 and 9 list the seven lineage names and then collapse them into two parties. Jacob 1:13 had established the same seven about five hundred years before Christ, and 4 Nephi 1:36 to 38 shows them coming back into use after two centuries in which nobody used any of them.

world_behind.title: The withdrawal is described in stages
world_behind.text: Verse 13 removes the disciples and the miracles, and verse 14 removes the gifts and the Holy Ghost. 4 Nephi 1:14 had the twelve chosen by Jesus already gone save the three who tarry; this is the point at which the three go too, and the record dates it inside four years of peace.

world_behind.title: He is silenced
world_behind.text: Verses 16 and 17 say twice that he was forbidden to preach. Mormon 3:2 has the Lord tell him to cry repentance to the same people about thirty years later, so the prohibition was for a season and the record marks both ends of it.

words.text: Serious, steady, not given to excess. Treated at Alma 37:47. The record uses the word four times, twice in this chapter, and the King James Bible twelve.
Marks cut into metal, and the records made that way. Treated at Alma 63:12. It appears twelve times in the record, and the King James Bible five, all in Exodus.
To make an attempt, to try. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible not at all. Verse 16 uses it of preaching he was not allowed to do.
To overrun, to be present in troubling numbers. The record uses the word twice, here and at 3 Nephi 1:27, while the King James Bible has none. Verse 18 uses it of the Gadianton robbers.
Unable to be held. Treated at Helaman 13:31. Its count is four times, three of them in that Helaman chapter, in this book, while the King James Bible three.
Attempts to gain power by hidden arts. It turns up twice, here and at Alma 1:32, against five in the King James Bible.
Practices of magic. This record has it once, here, and none in the King James Bible. Verse 19 places it third in a list of three.

phrases.term: I, Mormon, make a record of the things which I have both seen and heard
phrases.text: The whole book described in one clause. Seeing and hearing are the two sources he claims.

phrases.term: And call it the Book of Mormon
phrases.text: The title given by the man who made it. The naming happens in the first sentence.

phrases.term: I perceive that thou art a sober child, and art quick to observe
phrases.text: The reason a ten-year-old is chosen. Ammaron names two qualities and neither is learning.

phrases.term: When ye are about twenty and four years old
phrases.text: An instruction with a fourteen-year delay. The boy is told to remember until then.

phrases.term: Ye shall engrave on the plates of Nephi all the things that ye have observed
phrases.text: The assignment is to record his own observation. Verse 2 had already called that his gift.

phrases.term: The people were as numerous almost, as it were the sand of the sea
phrases.text: The land at its fullest. What follows in this book is the emptying of it.

phrases.term: The Lord did take away his beloved disciples
phrases.text: The three of 3 Nephi 28 removed. Verse 13 gives iniquity as the reason.

phrases.term: There were no gifts from the Lord, and the Holy Ghost did not come upon any
phrases.text: The withdrawal stated at its widest. Not one person is excepted.

phrases.term: I was visited of the Lord, and tasted and knew of the goodness of Jesus
phrases.text: A personal exception in the same chapter as the general withdrawal. He is fifteen.

phrases.term: My mouth was shut, and I was forbidden that I should preach
phrases.text: The silencing stated in two ways. Verse 17 gives the reason as the hardness of their hearts.

phrases.term: But I did remain among them
phrases.text: One clause on what he did with the silence. He stayed where he could not speak.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: The record names itself, once
verses.text: The opening sentence supplies a title in the first person: "I, Mormon, make a record of the things which I have both seen and heard, and call it the Book of Mormon." The phrase "Book of Mormon" appears in this verse and in no other verse of the whole record. A volume that has been running for five hundred pages under other headings gets its name here, from the man whose name it takes, in a sentence that also states his qualification as a witness of what he reports.

verses.label: v. 2–5
verses.title: Two parentheses carrying the writer's whole biography
verses.text: The record hands over the facts about its author inside brackets: "(I being about ten years of age, and I began to be learned somewhat after the manner of the learning of my people)" at verse 2, and "(and my father's name was Mormon)" at verse 5. Age, schooling, and parentage, all of it parenthetical. Everything else in the passage belongs to Ammaron's instructions, so the only autobiography in the chapter's opening is the material the sentences could have done without.

verses.label: v. 3–4
verses.title: A commission with a date, a place, and a limit
verses.text: The instruction is specific on all three: wait until "twenty and four years old," go "to the land Antum, unto a hill which shall be called Shim," and take the plates of Nephi "and the remainder shall ye leave in the place where they are." A boy of ten is given a task fourteen years out, with an inventory restriction attached. The record reports the appointment being kept at Mormon 2:17, in the year 345 and near the city of Jashon, "according to the word of Ammaron." What it does not report is Mormon reaching the hill Shim at twenty-four, so the errand is confirmed and its stated date is not.

verses.label: v. 15–17
verses.title: A prohibition on preaching, stated twice
verses.text: The record gives the ban in verse 16, "my mouth was shut, and I was forbidden that I should preach unto them," and then again in verse 17, "I was forbidden to preach unto them, because of the hardness of their hearts." Two statements of the same prohibition in consecutive verses, with different reasons attached: wilful rebellion in one and hardness of heart in the other. Verse 15 has just recorded a personal visitation at fifteen, so the record places the calling and the silencing side by side and never resolves the tension.

chapter.title: The record is named before it is made
chapter.text: Verse 1 gives the title and verse 4 gives the assignment. The reader is told what this is from the first line.

chapter.title: A child is chosen for watching, not for learning
chapter.text: Verse 2 names sober and quick to observe. Verse 2 mentions his learning in parentheses and Ammaron does not cite it.

chapter.title: The charge sits unused for fourteen years
chapter.text: Verse 3 sets the date at twenty-four. Most of the assignment is waiting.

chapter.title: The lineage names return in force
chapter.text: Verses 8 and 9 use all seven, then reduce them to two. 4 Nephi 1:17 had erased every one of them.

chapter.title: The gifts go before the wars do
chapter.text: Verses 13 and 14 come before the long decline. The book treats the spiritual loss as the first casualty.

chapter.title: One boy is excepted
chapter.text: Verse 15 has him visited in the same paragraph that says the Holy Ghost came upon no one. The record does not smooth this over.

chapter.title: He is stopped from doing the obvious thing
chapter.text: Verse 16 has him forbidden to preach. The one useful response available to him is closed off.

chapter.title: The chapter ends on fulfilled prophecy
chapter.text: Verse 19 names Abinadi and Samuel the Lamanite. Words spoken centuries apart land in the same sentence.

applications.title: Name the thing you are making
applications.text: Mormon's opening sentence says he records what he has seen and heard, and calls it the Book of Mormon. Deciding what a piece of work is and giving it a name is what turns a pile of notes into a project.

applications.title: Notice who is watching
applications.text: Ammaron picked a ten-year-old for being observant. The quality that qualified him is available at any age.

applications.title: Carry an assignment you cannot act on yet
applications.text: Fourteen years passed between the charge and the doing. Remembering is sometimes the whole of the work for a long time.

applications.title: Peak size is not peak health
applications.text: The whole face of the land was covered with buildings and the people were almost as the sand of the sea, and the war starts in the next verse. The two measurements are different, and the chapter puts them side by side on purpose.

applications.title: Expect the gifts to go quietly
applications.text: No announcement, just absence. What is lost first is often noticed last.

applications.title: Fifteen is old enough
applications.text: Mormon reports that he was fifteen years of age, of a sober mind, and was visited of the Lord. The record gives an age rather than a stage of life, and the age is younger than most people would guess.

applications.title: Stay when you cannot speak
applications.text: He was forbidden to preach and remained among them. Presence is a form of service when speech is closed.

applications.title: Old warnings can be filling in around you
applications.text: The sorceries and witchcrafts of that year are described as fulfilling the words of Abinadi and of Samuel the Lamanite. Recognizing that you are living inside something already written about changes what you do next.

questions.text: What have I seen and heard that only I can record?
Am I quick to observe, or only quick to speak?
What was I told years ago that I am still meant to do?
What gift have I stopped expecting?
When did I last taste and know the goodness of Jesus?
What have I been unable to say, and to whom?
What am I holding that keeps turning slippery?
